segments.text: Christopher Demanche, Development Coordination. Agenda item 2 is rez 26-08. This is a request to rezone 17700 West Courtney Campbell Causeway from planned development allowing mixed use residential multiple family and hotel uses to planned development to allow for hotel residential multiple family and all commercial general uses. I'll turn it over to Planning Commission Staff. Danny Collins with your Planning Commission Staff. I was sworn in. Our first case tonight is in the Westshore Planning district. The subject site is within evacuation zone a. It is also within the coastal high hazard area. Here is our adopted future land use map. The subject site is designated as urban mixed use 60, which is a high density land use category, encourages mixed use and a broad range of uses. The surrounding area is predominantly UMU 60. There is some CMU 35 to the east of the subject site. Just for reference, this is the former godfrey hotel site and council approved a rezoning just to the south of the site on the old rusty pelican site I believe it was in 2025. The Planning Commission Staff found the request to be comparable and compatible with the surrounding area. The surrounding area includes a mix of uses including multifamily condos and like commercial development. More intensive development is generally located south of the Courtney Campbell Causeway where we have less intensive development to the north of the causeway. The proposed 220-foot building height would be compatible with the surrounding development pattern in the area. As mentioned in 2025, the rusty pelican site, which is located here, rusty pelican site located to the south of the site was approved for the same 220-foot building height as proposed through this application. Applicant also ventured into a bonus provision agreement with the city. Staff found that the request addresses the mixed use centers and corridor design policies in the comprehensive plan. The proposed design places the building close to the right-of-way and connects the building entrances to internal sidewalks and crosswalks. Connections are also provided -- provide access to courtney Campbell trail along the right-of-way. The site also provides bicycle parking and landscape plan proposes shade trees along the right-of-way and throughout the site. These design features are supported by the comprehensive plan. Finally, the request advances several housing policies as well as infill policies in the plan. The plan encourages residential development on vacant and underutilized parcels to support Tampa's housing needs. Staff has noted a minor correction to the site area that needs to be made between first and second reading. That correction is included on the city's revision sheet. Based on these considerations and with that revision, the Planning Commission Staff finds the request consistent with the City Of Tampa comprehensive plan, and that concludes my presentation.
